english.title: Use a motor vehicle with speedometer obscured

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: ROAD VEHICLES CONSTRUCTION AND USE REGULATIONS 1986

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), when its speedometer was not kept free from obstruction which might prevent its being easily read.
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 36(1) of the Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986, section 42 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
use on a road a motor vehicle
fitted with an instrument for indicating speed
which was not kept free from obstruction which might prevent its being easily read.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 36(2) defines 'all material times' and defines certain times as not being material.
(ii) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
(iii) See also offence wordings: H660, H661, H662, H664 and H665.
english.standardstatementoffacts: At **(..SPECIFY TIME..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) the defendant used on **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..) **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..) when it was fitted with a speedometer which was not kept free from obstruction which might prevent its being easily read.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

A fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale if in respect of goods vehicle or vehicle adapted to carry more than eight passengers.

Fixed penalty ticket - Fifty pounds.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
